chapter_name: History and Structure of Tabla & Pakhawaj
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the origin stories of these great instruments! Understand how Tabla and Pakhawaj were created, the names of their structural parts, and how they produce sound.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pakhawaj is an ancient instrument, considered a variant of the Mridang. It is traditionally played with Dhrupad and Dhamar vocal styles. It is hollowed out of a single block of wood and covered with leather on both sides.

Legend has it that in the 13th-14th century, Amir Khusro cut the Pakhawaj (or Mridang) into two halves to invent the Tabla. The left part is called 'Bayan' (Dagga) and the right part is called 'Dayan' (Tabla).
The right Tabla is usually made of wood (Sheesham or Khirni), and the left (Bayan) is made of clay, copper, or brass. The leather stretched over the top is called the 'Puri'.

The Puri (leather top) has three main parts: 1. Syahi (the black center made of iron filings), 2. Lav/Maidan (the area outside the Syahi), 3. Chaanti/Kinaar (the outermost edge). Striking these different areas produces different syllables.

Leather straps (Baddi) are used to tighten the skin. Round wooden blocks called 'Gattas' are inserted between the straps of the right Tabla. They are hammered up or down to tune the pitch of the Tabla.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 Draw and Label the Tabla
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a picture of a Dayan (Tabla) and Bayan (Dagga). Accurately label the Syahi (black dot), Maidan, Chaanti, Gajra (braided edge), Baddi, and Gatta. This will help you immensely in both theory and practical exams!

exam_tips: 📌 The definitions and functions of various Tabla parts (Syahi, Lav, Chaanti, Baddi, Gatta) are frequently asked in exams.
📌 Always include the legend of Amir Khusro cutting the Pakhawaj into two when writing about the history and origin of the Tabla.
📌 Remember the distinction: Pakhawaj (single wooden block, used in Dhrupad) vs. Tabla (two separate drums, used in Khayal singing).
quick_recap: ⭐ The left Tabla (Bayan) produces a deep, resonating bass sound, while the right Tabla (Dayan) produces a sharp, melodic treble sound.
⭐ The 'Syahi' is a mixture of iron filings, flour, and glue applied in layers to give the sound its unique resonance.
